signature: bool validatePageToHostMessage(const BridgeMessage& message, QString* error = nullptr) const
behavior: Validates one page-to-host bridge envelope against the configured size limit, protocol version, allowed message type, required payload field types, and additional-field policy. This directly replaces validateBridgeMessage; no compatibility overload is retained.
parameters: message: const BridgeMessage& [non-null borrowed immutable envelope]; error: QString* [nullable borrowed output, written with rejection detail or cleared]
return_contract: bool is true exactly when the message satisfies pageToHostSchemas and the common bridge limits.
error_contract: Expected rejection is false with a stable human-readable detail when error is non-null; no implementation exceptions escape.
null_contract: error absence is represented only by nullptr; message and bool result are non-null.
ownership_contract: message is borrowed for the call; error is borrowed for the call; policy owns its copied configuration.
mutation_contract: Read-only policy operation; may replace the caller-owned error string; no other caller-visible mutation.
placement_rationale: WebViewPolicy owns bridge admission rules shared by all platform backends.
implementation_evidence: Declaration and typed directional schema: src/webview/WebViewPolicy.h; implementation: src/webview/WebViewPolicy.cpp; direction/type/extra/size tests: tests/JsonMessageTests.cpp; platform callers: src/platform/macos/WkWebView.mm and src/platform/windows/WebView2View.cpp.
reconciliation_evidence: Compared WebViewPolicy.h and WebViewPolicy.cpp with the planned contract; searched system-webview, samples, tests, and Texteasy for validateBridgeMessage, bridgeSchemas, requiredPayloadKeys, and all new symbols; every page ingress uses validatePageToHostMessage and no production old API remains.
impact_review: Source-breaking replacement affects demo, platform backends, tests, and Texteasy; all known source consumers were migrated. Qt 5.15/C++17 framework build and core tests pass; Texteasy consumes the installed headers under C++20.
cognitive_load_review: One direction-specific operation takes one immutable BridgeMessage and one optional error output; schema types, strict-extra policy, size, version, and allowed type are declared in WebViewPolicyConfig; no mode flag or hidden direction selection remains.
placement_review: WebViewPolicy remains the single owner of shared bridge admission rules; macOS and Windows backends only decode envelopes and invoke the public directional policy method.

signature: void sendMessage(const BridgeMessage& message, MessageCompletion completion = {})
behavior: Attempts to deliver one host-to-page message only when the view is open, the committed document is bridge-authorized, and the message satisfies hostToPageSchemas. Exactly one supplied completion is invoked with the outcome. MessageCompletion is a namespace-level public type.
parameters: message: const BridgeMessage& [non-null borrowed immutable envelope]; completion: MessageCompletion [optional owned callable]
return_contract: void; delivery outcome is reported once through completion when supplied.
error_contract: Expected outcomes use MessageError: Closed, NavigationChanged, Rejected, or None; platform failures are translated into MessageResult detail.
null_contract: completion absence is represented only by an empty std::function; message and MessageResult are non-null values.
ownership_contract: message is borrowed until serialization during the call; completion is copied/moved into asynchronous delivery and owns its captures.
mutation_contract: May enqueue JavaScript delivery; does not mutate the input; pending completion is invalidated predictably by navigation or close.
placement_rationale: IWebView owns delivery to its current native document; policy owns admission.
implementation_evidence: Declaration and namespace-level MessageCompletion: src/webview/IWebView.h and src/webview/WebViewTypes.h; authorization/validation implementations: src/platform/macos/WkWebView.mm and src/platform/windows/WebView2View.cpp; macOS rejection/delivery coverage: tests/WkViewTests.mm.
reconciliation_evidence: Re-read IWebView.h, WebViewTypes.h, WkWebView.mm, and WebView2View.cpp; searched every sendMessage and MessageCompletion caller in system-webview and Texteasy. The namespace-level callback type and host-to-page policy behavior agree with the declaration and all consumers.
impact_review: MessageCompletion moved from IWebView scope to webview scope, so source callers using the nested alias must migrate; the known Texteasy caller was updated. Windows now rejects unauthorized or invalid outgoing messages like macOS; no compatibility alias remains.
cognitive_load_review: One send operation accepts one typed envelope and one optional completion. Closed, navigation-changed, rejected, unsupported, and successful outcomes share MessageResult; no overload, mode selector, nullable message, or platform exception leaks.
placement_review: IWebView owns delivery to its committed native document; WebViewPolicy owns admission. The consumer wrapper depends only on installed public headers and delegates transport unchanged.

behavior: Receives page-to-host messages only after main-document origin, document token, common bridge limits, and pageToHostSchemas validation succeed. An empty callback suppresses dispatch safely.
parameters: message: const BridgeMessage& [non-null borrowed immutable validated envelope]
return_contract: void; no delivery acknowledgment is exposed to the page.
error_contract: Rejected or malformed page messages are dropped before invocation; callback exceptions follow the existing C++ callback contract.
null_contract: callback absence is represented only by an empty std::function; message is non-null.
ownership_contract: message is borrowed only for callback duration; callback owns any data it copies.
mutation_contract: Invokes caller code synchronously on the platform event path; framework state is not exposed for mutation.
placement_rationale: WebViewHostCallbacks is the declared host event surface; platform backends are responsible for admission before dispatch.
implementation_evidence: Callback declaration: src/webview/WebViewTypes.h; guarded directional dispatch: src/platform/macos/WkWebView.mm and src/platform/windows/WebView2View.cpp; page dispatch coverage: tests/WkViewTests.mm.
reconciliation_evidence: Re-read WebViewTypes.h and both platform dispatch implementations; searched every callback assignment and invocation in framework tests, demo, and Texteasy. Both backends check callback presence and page-to-host validation before invoking it; no stale bidirectional validator remains.
impact_review: Existing callback signature is retained, but its admitted message set is now direction-specific and typed. Demo, macOS test, and Texteasy page schemas were migrated; malformed envelopes and rejected schema messages are dropped before consumer code.
cognitive_load_review: The host receives one immutable, already-validated BridgeMessage or no call. Callback absence is one empty std::function representation; no direction flag, transport object, policy internals, or lifetime token reaches the consumer.
placement_review: WebViewHostCallbacks remains the public event owner; native backends own origin/token/envelope checks and policy admission immediately before dispatch.
